title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: Objections 4–5 — Achan; other heads (Noah/Abraham)
pass_a_gloss: The body is not one member but many; the foot is of the body though not the head, and what the foot does is imputed to the whole body too. So when God considered his people as one body in the desert and was angry with the whole for one Achan—who was not that people's head—then if all men coalesce with Adam into one body, not one sin of one Adam but all Adam's and all other men's sins would have to be imputed to the whole, which neither the Apostle nor the opponent according to the Apostle allows. Fourth: why not fit this likeness also to other stocks—Noah as head of the second world, Abraham of the Israelites, and so of the rest—whence a great mass of sins to be imputed would arise? Adam is called head and compared to a king by the origin-relation he acquired to posterity by generating, not merely because he was first. Fifth: if enemies kill someone they know was alien to the war in will and deed, that seems monstrous; otherwise the King's war-mind is presumed the subjects' mind, yet deserters and those who surrender are usually spared.
pass_b_english: For the body is not one member but many: and if the foot is not the head, it does not follow that the foot is not of the body. And what the head does is imputed to the whole body, and also what the foot does. So when God considered his people as one body in the desert, he was angry with the whole people for one Achan, who was not that people's head. If therefore all men coalesce with Adam into one body, not one sin of one Adam but all Adam's and all other men's sins must be imputed to the whole body. Yet neither the Apostle nor you according to the Apostle approve that. Fourth, what stands in the way of fitting this likeness also to other stocks and parents respecting their posterity? For example, why should Noah not also be head of the second world, Abraham of the Israelites, and so of the rest—whence a great mass of sins to be imputed would arise? For Adam is called head and compared to a king not because he was the first man, but because we draw origin from him. He is not referred to us by negation of relation to a prior, but by the relation he acquired to posterity by generating. Fifth, if someone falls into enemies' hands whom they know for certain was alien to the war in will and deed and did not consent to it, if they kill that innocent man they seem to me monstrous and cruel. Otherwise the mind of the King making war is presumed to be the mind of all subjects. But deserters and those who surrender are usually spared.
source_text: Corpus enim non est unum membrum, sed multa: nec si pes caput non est, consequens est pedem non esse ex corpore. Imputatur autem toti corpori non modo quod caput facit, sed etiam quod pes. Itaque cum populum suum Deus consideraret ut unum corpus in deserto, toti populo ob unius Achan, qui populi illius caput non erat, iratus est. Si ergo omnes homines coalescunt cum Adamo in unum corpus, non unius Adami unum peccatum, sed omnia Adami, omnia aliorum hominum peccata toti corpori imputanda sunt. Quod tamen nec Apostolus, nec tu secundum Apostolum probas. Quarto, quid obstat quominus haec similitudo accommodetur etiam aliis stirpibus & parentibus respectu posterorum? Exempli causa, cur Noachus etiam non sit secundi mundi caput, Abrahamus Israelitarum, & ita de reliquis; unde magna exurget moles peccatorum imputandorum? Caput enim dicitur Adamus, & regi comparatur, non quia primus homo fuit, sed quia ab eo ducimus originem. Negatione relationis ad priorem ad nos minime refertur, sed relatione, quam generando sibi acquisivit, ad posteros. Quinto, si quis in manus hostium incidat quem certo noverint a bello fuisse & voluntate, & opere alienum, nec in id consensisse, hunc si interficiunt innocentem, mihi immanes & crudeles esse videntur. Alioqui qua Regis est mens bellum inferentis, eadem praesumitur esse mens omnium subditorum. Transfugis autem, iisque qui se dedunt, parci solet.
